correctness.rationale: The complete lattice-point lists agree with Figure 1.4. Reducing the six exponent pairs modulo seven gives six distinct characters for each code. They are independent: a reduced polynomial of degree at most six in each variable vanishing on the 7×7 grid is zero by univariate interpolation in each variable. The coordinate map phi(x,y)=(x^(-1),x^(-3)y) squares to the identity, and the paired weights x^3 and (x^(-1))^3 multiply to one. The weighted pullback sends (a,b) to (3-a-3b,b): the four horizontal exponents reverse, (0,1) stays fixed, and (0,-1) becomes (6,-1)=(-1,-1) modulo seven. Thus it sends precisely one basis of the evaluation code onto the other. The edge-step gcd sums give four and three boundary lattice points, ruling out integral affine unimodular equivalence. Independent exact replay in /workspace/replays/4.py passed the lattice-point, area, boundary, reduced-exponent and 49-coordinate weight/permutation checks. The frozen checker and recorded output were inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: The equivalence is on evaluation coordinates, not an equality of formal Laurent section spaces. The conclusion is for F_8 and completes the relevant dimension-six classification in the original theorem's field range, not every dimension or field.
